en.commentary: I rank running shoes by three numbers that survive contact with reality: cost per mile, how many types of run a single pair can cover, and whether the fit still works at 500 miles. Judged that way the Asics Novablast 6 is the shoe of 2026. It costs $150, its FF Turbo forefoot stays lively deep into a shoe's life, and the ASICSGRIP outsole holds rubber long enough to push the per-mile cost under thirty cents. That combination is why it beats shoes priced $20 to $110 above it. The market moved in the same direction this year. Running footwear grew 8.9 percent while lifestyle footwear slipped 0.9 percent, which tells me buyers are spending on performance and comparing specs before they buy. Nike still holds about 24 percent share, and Hoka, On, New Balance and Adidas are all pushing into the daily trainer slot, so the top of this list is genuinely contested for the first time in years. Super shoes deserve a clear answer, because they are now the default at big-city marathons: 64 percent of Chicago finishers and 62 percent in New York raced in carbon plates. The physics is real. Supercritical PEBA returns 85 to 90 percent of the energy you put into it against 55 to 65 percent for standard EVA, and the published economy gain sits at 4 to 6 percent. The Vaporfly 4 and Adios Pro 4 sit at ranks 9 and 10 here because this list rewards versatility and cost per mile, and a racing shoe spends most of its life in a box. Buy one when you have a goal race and a training shoe already in rotation. One last thing worth knowing before you click buy: your shoe budget is better spent on two $150 trainers than one $260 racer if you run four or more times a week. Rotating two pairs lets foam rebound between runs and stretches the life of both.

highlights.title: The Novablast 6 wins because $150 now buys the best ride in running
highlights.body: Asics dropped weight, reworked the upper and kept FF Turbo in the forefoot, and the result is a shoe that runs easy miles at 6:00 per kilometre and tempo intervals at 4:20 without feeling out of place at either end. The ASICSGRIP outsole is the part reviewers keep underrating: it still shows tread at the point where softer compounds are down to foam. At $150 and roughly 800 kilometres of usable life, the Novablast 6 lands near $0.19 per kilometre, the lowest figure on this list, and it does that while ranking top three on ride quality.

highlights.title: Vomero Plus is the correct answer for anyone running more than 60km a week
highlights.body: Full-length ZoomX under a max stack is the single most protective setup Nike sells for daily training, and high-mileage legs feel that on the fourth and fifth run of the week. It weighs about 273 grams in a men's US 10, which is remarkably light for the volume of foam involved. The $180 price buys cushioning depth that the $150 tier cannot physically match, and it is available in standard, wide and extra-wide, so the fit works for feet that get squeezed by narrow race-inspired uppers.

highlights.title: Super shoes are worth it above a certain pace, and the maths says where
highlights.body: A 4 to 6 percent economy gain scales with how much time you spend running, so a 3-hour marathoner banks roughly 7 to 10 minutes and a 5-hour marathoner banks a smaller share of a longer day while absorbing three to four times more load on the calves and plantar fascia. Carbon racers also last 250 to 400 kilometres against 700 to 800 for a daily trainer. At $260 that works out to about $0.87 per kilometre for the Vaporfly 4, roughly four times the Novablast 6. Buy one for a goal race, keep it for the goal race.

highlights.title: Fit beats brand loyalty, and width is where most online purchases go wrong
highlights.body: Sizing runs differently across these ten shoes by enough to change your size. Hoka and Brooks fit close to true, the Endorphin Speed 5 runs snug through the midfoot, and the Gel-Kayano 33 is the only premium shoe here offered in 2E and 4E as a normal stock item. If you have a wide forefoot, start with the Kayano 33, the Ghost 18 or the Vomero Plus, all of which ship in wide fits. Order two widths, run both on a treadmill, send one back. That single habit removes the most common reason people abandon a shoe at 100 kilometres.

zh-tw.commentary: 老實說，我挑跑鞋只看三件事：每公里成本、一雙能吃下多少種課表、還有跑到 800 公里時鞋還合不合腳。用這三個標準去排，2026 年的冠軍就是 ASICS Novablast 6。台灣定價 NT$4,580，FF Turbo 前掌到後期還是有彈性，ASICSGRIP 大底耐磨到可以把每公里成本壓到六塊台幣以內，這也是它能壓過那些貴上一兩千甚至三千塊對手的原因。今年市場的方向也很清楚，跑步鞋類年增 8.9%，生活風格鞋類反而掉了 0.9%，代表大家把鞋子的預算移到性能上，買之前也開始認真比規格。Nike 市佔還有 24% 左右，但 Hoka、On、New Balance、Adidas 全部往日常訓練鞋這一格擠，榜單前段這幾年來第一次真的有得吵。碳板鞋要不要買，這題我給明確答案。芝加哥馬拉松有 64% 的完賽者穿碳板鞋、紐約是 62%，它已經是大型賽事的預設值。物理上也站得住腳，超臨界 PEBA 的能量回饋率有 85% 到 90%，一般 EVA 只有 55% 到 65%，文獻上的跑步經濟性提升是 4% 到 6%。Vaporfly 4 跟 Adios Pro 4 在這份榜單排第 9 跟第 10，理由是我這份排名把泛用性跟每公里成本算得很重，而一雙競速鞋大部分時間都待在鞋盒裡。手上已經有訓練鞋、而且有目標賽事的人再買，這個順序才對。講真的，最後一個建議可能比選哪雙更重要：一週跑四次以上的人，把預算花在兩雙 NT$4,500 的訓練鞋上，會比壓在一雙 NT$7,600 的競速鞋划算。兩雙輪替讓中底有時間回彈，兩雙的壽命都會拉長。

highlights.title: Novablast 6 拿下第一，是因為 NT$4,580 現在買得到全榜最好的腳感
highlights.body: ASICS 這代把重量減下來、鞋面重做，前掌的 FF Turbo 留著，結果就是一雙配速 6:00 的輕鬆跑跟 4:20 的節奏跑都能跑的鞋，兩端都不會覺得勉強。ASICSGRIP 大底是評測圈一直低估的部分，跑到別家鞋已經磨到露中底的里程，它的紋路還在。以 NT$4,580 換算大約 800 公里的可用壽命，每公里成本落在 5.7 元左右，是這十雙裡最低的，而且它的腳感評分還排在前三。

highlights.title: 週跑量 60 公里以上的人，Vomero Plus 就是那個答案
highlights.body: 整片 ZoomX 配上厚底，是 Nike 目前在日常訓練這一格最有保護力的組合，跑量大的腿在一週的第四趟、第五趟課表會很明顯感覺到差別。男鞋 US 10 大約 273 公克，以這個泡棉厚度來說算很輕。NT$5,800 買到的緩衝深度，NT$4,500 那一階在物理上做不出來，而且它有標準楦、寬楦跟超寬楦，腳背高或腳掌寬的人不用硬塞窄鞋面。

highlights.title: 碳板鞋值不值得，要看你的配速，而且這筆帳可以算出來
highlights.body: 4% 到 6% 的經濟性提升是跟著跑步時間放大的，全馬 3 小時完賽的人大概省下 7 到 10 分鐘，5 小時完賽的人拿到的比例較低，但小腿跟足底承受的負荷卻是平常訓練鞋的三到四倍。碳板鞋的壽命只有 250 到 400 公里，一般訓練鞋是 700 到 800 公里。Vaporfly 4 台灣賣 NT$7,600，換算下來每公里大約 22 元，是 Novablast 6 的四倍。有目標賽事再買，買了就留給那場比賽穿。

highlights.title: 合腳比品牌重要，而網購跑鞋出錯最多的地方就是楦頭
highlights.body: 這十雙的版型差異大到會影響尺寸選擇。Hoka 跟 Brooks 接近正常尺碼，Endorphin Speed 5 的中足偏包覆，GEL-KAYANO 33 是這裡唯一把 2E 與 4E 當常態庫存供應的高階鞋，台灣通路同步有貨。腳掌偏寬的人從 Kayano 33、Ghost 18 或 Vomero Plus 開始挑，這三雙都有寬楦。建議一次訂兩個楦頭，在跑步機上各跑一趟再退掉一雙。光是養成這個習慣，就能避掉大多數人跑到 100 公里就把鞋冰起來的下場。

en.commentary: August is a heavy release month and two arrivals on August 1 are worth knowing about even though neither changes this board today. Brooks launched the Hyperion Elite 6, its current super shoe, and Hoka released the updated Tecton X with a more durable Matryx Micro upper and an extra top lacing eyelet, a shoe Francesco Puppi wore to second place in his 100 mile debut at Western States. Both are specialist tools rather than daily trainers, which is exactly why this list stays focused on shoes that handle the majority of a runner's weekly mileage. The ASICS Novablast 6 holds first at 9.2 because it is the most versatile shoe here. It has enough foam to be comfortable on an easy hour, enough responsiveness to handle a tempo section without feeling mushy, and a midsole that holds its properties past 500 kilometres. Most runners need one shoe that does everything well rather than three shoes that each do one thing perfectly, and the Novablast 6 is the best answer to that need. Nike Vomero Plus second at 9.0 offers the most cushioning per gram for high mileage weeks. Brooks Ghost 18 third at 8.9 is the neutral daily trainer I recommend to new runners, because its predictability makes it very hard to get wrong. For Taiwan, my standing note: buy a half size up from your normal fit and shop in the evening, since heat and humidity here cause noticeably more foot swelling than the conditions most sizing guides assume. No rank or score changes today.

highlights.title: One versatile shoe beats three specialists for most runners
highlights.body: The Novablast 6 handles an easy hour comfortably, holds up through a tempo section without feeling mushy, and keeps its midsole properties past 500 kilometres. Unless you are racing frequently, a rotation of specialist shoes adds cost and complexity without adding fitness. That versatility is the whole case for first place at 9.2.

highlights.title: August's new arrivals are race tools, not daily trainers
highlights.body: Brooks launched the Hyperion Elite 6 and Hoka released the updated Tecton X on August 1, both excellent within their specific purpose. Super shoes and trail racers earn their place in a rotation only after a reliable daily trainer is already covering the weekly mileage. Buy the base of the pyramid first.

highlights.title: Shop in the evening and size up half a step in Taiwan
highlights.body: Heat and humidity here cause noticeably more foot swelling than the conditions most sizing charts assume, and a shoe that fits perfectly in an air conditioned shop at noon can feel tight on a July evening run. Trying shoes late in the day with the socks you actually run in prevents the most common fit mistake.

highlights.title: Midsole durability is the specification nobody publishes
highlights.body: Foam that loses its rebound at 300 kilometres costs far more per kilometre than a shoe that holds its properties past 500, regardless of the sticker price. Judge value by cost per kilometre rather than cost per pair. That calculation moves durable trainers like the Novablast 6 and the Ghost 18 up considerably.

zh-tw.commentary:

Brooks 推出了 Hyperion Elite 6，也就是它現行的超級跑鞋，Hoka 則發表了改款的 Tecton X，換上更耐磨的 Matryx Micro 鞋面並多加一個上方鞋帶孔，Francesco Puppi 就是穿這雙在 Western States 的百英里首戰拿下第二名。

這兩雙都是專門工具而不是日常訓練鞋，而這正好說明了為什麼這份榜單要聚焦在能吃下跑者每週大部分里程的鞋款上。

ASICS Novablast 6 續坐第一 9.2，因為它是榜上最全能的。輕鬆跑一小時夠舒服、切進節奏跑也夠回彈不會軟爛、中底過了 500 公里仍保持特性。

說真的，多數跑者需要的是一雙什麼都做得不錯的鞋，而不是三雙各自把一件事做到完美的鞋，而 Novablast 6 是這個需求最好的答案。

Nike Vomero Plus 第二 9.0，大里程週每公克緩衝最多。Brooks Ghost 18 第三 8.9，新手我都推它，因為它的可預測性讓你很難買錯。

給台灣跑者的老提醒，比平常大半號，而且傍晚去買。台灣的濕熱造成的腳部腫脹，比多數尺寸指南所假設的條件明顯得多。今天名次分數不動。

highlights.title: 對多數跑者來說，一雙全能鞋勝過三雙專科鞋
highlights.body: Novablast 6 輕鬆跑一小時很舒服、切節奏跑不會軟爛、中底過了 500 公里還保持特性。除非你經常比賽，否則一整套專門鞋只會增加花費與複雜度，不會增加體能。這份全能性就是第一名 9.2 的全部理由。

highlights.title: 八月的新品是比賽工具，不是日常訓練鞋
highlights.body: Brooks 的 Hyperion Elite 6 與 Hoka 改款的 Tecton X 都在 8 月 1 日到位，在各自的用途上都很優秀。超級跑鞋跟越野競速鞋要進入鞋櫃輪換，前提是已經有一雙可靠的日常訓練鞋在吃週里程。先把金字塔底座買好。

highlights.title: 在台灣，傍晚去買、比平常大半號
highlights.body: 台灣的濕熱造成的腳部腫脹，比多數尺寸表所假設的條件明顯得多，中午在冷氣房裡試起來剛好的鞋，七月傍晚跑起來就會覺得緊。挑一天傍晚、穿你真正跑步的襪子去試，就能避開最常見的尺寸失誤。

highlights.title: 中底耐用度是沒人公布的規格
highlights.body: 一雙在 300 公里就失去回彈的泡棉，不管標價多少，每公里成本都遠高於能撐過 500 公里的鞋。用每公里成本來評估價值，不要用每雙的價格。這個算法會把 Novablast 6 跟 Ghost 18 這類耐操的訓練鞋往上推很多。

en.commentary: August is delivering one of the busiest release windows this category has seen, with three significant shoes landing inside two weeks: the Brooks Hyperion Elite 6 on August 1, New Balance's first genuinely plated Rebel, and Topo's debut super shoe. I have read the early testing on the Hyperion Elite 6 and it reads like the first Brooks racer that belongs in the conversation, built on a reworked PEBA DNA Gold midsole with more toe spring and a steeper plate angle. That is real news for anyone who has wanted to race in Brooks and could not justify it. None of it changes my top of the table today, and I want to explain why. ASICS Novablast 6 holds first at 9.2 because it is the shoe I recommend when someone tells me they own one pair. It handles easy miles, tempo work and the occasional long run at a price that leaves room for a second pair later. Nike Vomero Plus stays second at 9.0 on ride quality at 9.6, which is the plushest daily cushioning I have run in this year. Brooks Ghost 18 is third at 8.9 and earns it on durability at 9.5, the best cost per mile in this list. Here is my honest position on super shoes: Vaporfly 4 sits ninth at 7.9 and Adizero Adios Pro 4 tenth at 7.7 despite ride scores of 9.8 and 9.5, because a shoe with roughly 150 usable race miles is a race day tool rather than a rotation. Buy one only when you have a goal race on the calendar. No rank or score changes today.

highlights.title: Three notable releases land inside two weeks
highlights.body: The Brooks Hyperion Elite 6 arrived August 1 with a reworked PEBA DNA Gold midsole, more toe spring and a steeper plate angle. A plated New Balance Rebel and Topo's first super shoe follow close behind. Early testing calls the Brooks the brand's most credible racer yet, which is genuinely new territory for them.

highlights.title: Novablast 6 is the one pair answer
highlights.body: It covers easy miles, tempo sessions and the occasional long run without complaint, and it does so at a price that leaves budget for a second pair down the line. That range is exactly what a single shoe owner needs. It holds first at 9.2 with a category leading value score of 9.5.

highlights.title: Ghost 18 wins on cost per mile
highlights.body: A durability score of 9.5 is the highest here, and durability is the number that decides your real annual spend on running. If you log consistent weekly volume in a shoe that lasts noticeably longer, the price difference at checkout stops mattering within a few months. Third at 8.9, and my pick for high mileage weeks.

highlights.title: Super shoes belong to race day only
highlights.body: Vaporfly 4 and Adizero Adios Pro 4 post ride scores of 9.8 and 9.5, the two best in this ranking, and they still sit ninth and tenth. Roughly 150 usable race miles is the reason. Buy one when a goal race is already on your calendar, and let a daily trainer carry the training block.

zh-tw.commentary:
八月是這個品類近年最密集的發表窗口，兩週內連續落地三雙重要的鞋：8 月 1 日的 Brooks Hyperion Elite 6、New Balance 第一雙真正加碳板的 Rebel，還有 Topo 的初代競速鞋。

我看了 Hyperion Elite 6 的早期實測，這確實是 Brooks 第一雙有資格被放進競速鞋對話裡的作品，中底換成重新調配的 PEBA DNA Gold，前掌翹度加大，碳板角度也更陡。對那些一直想穿 Brooks 比賽、卻始終找不到理由的人來說，這是真消息。

不過今天榜首沒有動，我想說明理由。

ASICS Novablast 6 續坐第一 9.2，因為當有人跟我說他只打算買一雙，我推薦的就是它。輕鬆跑、節奏跑、偶爾拉個長距離它都吃得下，價格還留得下買第二雙的空間。

Nike Vomero Plus 第二 9.0，腳感 9.6，是我今年跑過最軟彈的日常緩衝。

Brooks Ghost 18 第三 8.9，耐用度 9.5 全榜最高，等於每公里成本最低。

What I want to say this week concerns how people choose running shoes, because the most common approach produces the wrong answer.

Buyers pick based on reviews of the shoe. The better approach is to pick based on what you are training for. A daily trainer needs to absorb high mileage comfortably and last five hundred kilometres. A tempo shoe needs to feel responsive at threshold pace. A racing shoe optimises for one goal event and gives up durability to do it. Buying a racing shoe for daily training wears out an expensive shoe quickly and gives you a harsher ride than you want.

The ASICS Novablast 6 holds first at 9.2 because it does the daily training job better than anything else here, with enough cushioning for long runs and enough responsiveness to pick up the pace.

One practical note. Replace shoes at around five hundred to eight hundred kilometres depending on your weight and surface. Midsole foam compresses long before the outsole looks worn, so visual inspection underestimates how used a shoe is.

台灣跑者有個很實際的裝備問題：鞋子乾不了。濕度高的季節，一雙鞋跑完隔天還是濕的，中底泡棉在濕的狀態下回彈也回不來，鞋墊還會養出味道。所以兩雙輪替在台灣算必需品，跑完抽出鞋墊、塞報紙、放通風處，比買鞋墊除臭劑有效多了。

Novablast 6 守住第一，就是因為它一雙可以扛下大部分訓練，高中底、回彈好，輕鬆跑、長距離、節奏跑都能用，美國售價 150 美元，是我榜上性價比最高的日常訓練鞋。想輪替第二雙的話，換色清倉是最划算的時機。

最後提醒夜跑的朋友，天黑得越來越早，反光材料放在腳踝和手腕，駕駛的眼睛對會動的反光最敏感。
